nodes.name: NF pretreatment
nodes.procedure: A piece of Ni foam (NF) was first dipped in diluted hydrochloric acid to remove the oxide films on the surface, followed by sonication in acetone for 15 min and finally cleaned by ethanol and deionized water for several times before use.

unit_operations.name: Acid dipping
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: dipped in diluted hydrochloric acid to remove the oxide films on the surface

unit_operations.name: Rinsing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: cleaned by ethanol and deionized water for several times

nodes.source_text: Previous to the synthesis, a piece of Ni foam (NF) was first dipped in diluted hydrochloric acid... cleaned by ethanol and deionized water for several times before use.

nodes.name: CoFe-LDH/NF hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.5 mmol of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 0.5 mmol of Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 10 mmol of urea and 4 mmol NH4F were dissolved in 30 ml water at room temperature to form a yellow solution. The solution was subsequently transferred into a 50 ml Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave in which as-prepared NF was immersed into the solution, heating at 120 °C for 6 h. After the reaction, the NF was washed by ethanol and deionized water for several times and then dried at 60 °C for overnight in a vacuum drying oven.

nodes.name: NiFe-LDH electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The NiFe-LDH was grown onto the surface of CoFe-LDH nanosheets by electrodeposition in a three-electrode configuration using CoFe-LDH/NF as working electrode, Pt wire as counter electrode, Ag/AgCl as reference electrode. Aqueous electrolyte containing 0.15 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.15 M FeSO4·7H2O. Constant potential of -1.0 V vs Ag/AgCl applied for 50 s, 100 s, 200 s, 300 s to produce CoFe@NiFe-50/NF, CoFe@NiFe-100/NF, CoFe@NiFe-200/NF, CoFe@NiFe-300/NF respectively.

unit_operations.name: Electrolyte preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Aqueous solution containing 0.15 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.15 M FeSO4·7H2O was used as electrolyte

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the deposition was performed by applying a constant potential of -1.0 V vs Ag/AgCl for 50 s, 100 s, 200 s, 300 s, respectively

nodes.source_text: The NiFe-LDH was grown onto the surface of CoFe-LDH nanosheets by electrodeposition... denoted as CoFe@NiFe-50/NF, CoFe@NiFe-100/NF, CoFe@NiFe-200/NF, CoFe@NiFe-300/NF, respectively.

nodes.description: OER performance in O₂-saturated 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: In order to evaluate the OER activity, the hierarchical CoFe@NiFe/NF core-shell architectures was measured by using a standard three-electrode system in O₂-saturated 1.0 M KOH... CoFe@NiFe-200/NF core-shell architecture displays the remarkable catalytic with low η₁₀ of only 190 mV... Tafel slope of CoFe@NiFe-200/NF core-shell architecture is evaluated to be 45.71 mV dec⁻¹... CoFe@NiFe-200/NF exhibits much smaller R_ct (0.92 Ω)... CoFe@NiFe-200/NF possesses highest C_dl... calculated TOF of CoFe@NiFe-200/NF architecture is 11.9 s⁻¹... I-t curve shows... outstanding stable OER behavior with a constant overpotential after 30 h

nodes.description: HER performance in Ar-saturated 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The HER activity of samples was also investigated in a three-electrode system in Ar-saturated 1.0 M KOH... CoFe@NiFe-200/NF shows... low overpotential (η₁₀) of 240 mV... small Tafel slope of 88.88 mV dec⁻¹... R_ct = 3.74 Ω... CoFe@NiFe core-shell architectures possess the largest C_dl... calculated TOF value... is 15.7 s⁻¹... I-t curve... excellent stability for maintaining the original current density within continue 30 h

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in symmetrical two-electrode cell
nodes.source_text: the symmetrical two-electrode cell using CoFe@NiFe/NF as both the cathode and anode acquire only 1.59 V at the current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... the electrolytic potential hold steady within 24 h... the FE is calculated to be approximately 99.3 %... The H₂ or O₂ production rates are approximately 0.30 mmol h⁻¹ h⁻¹ and 0.15 mmol h⁻¹

nodes.description: Faradaic efficiency measurement for H₂ and O₂ evolution
nodes.source_text: Electrochemical H₂ and O₂ evolutions were measured... in 1.0 M KOH... the FE is calculated to be approximately 99.3 %. The H₂ or O₂ production rates are approximately 0.30 mmol h⁻¹ h⁻¹ and 0.15 mmol h⁻¹, respectively, with the atomic ratio of H₂ and O₂ being close to 2:1

nodes.characterization_summary: CoFe-LDH/NF exhibits nanosheets with smooth surfaces and ~50 nm thickness vertically grown on NF forming 3D arrays. CoFe@NiFe-200/NF shows NiFe-LDH nanosheets vertically deposited on CoFe-LDH forming hierarchical 'nanosheet-on-nanosheet' structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images (Fig. 2a, b) of CoFe-LDH/NF sample indicates that the CoFe-LDH nanosheets with smooth surface and thicknesses of around 50 nm were erectly growth on the NF substrate, forming 3D interconnected nanosheets arrays ... After electrodeposition, the NiFe-LDH nanosheets were erectly deposited on the CoFe-LDH nanosheet arrays substrate (Fig. 2c, d), forming well-defined hierarchical 'nanosheet on nanosheet' architecture.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoFe@NiFe-200/NF shows tiny NiFe-LDH nanosheets of ~6 nm thickness decorated on smooth CoFe-LDH nanosheet surface forming hierarchical core-shell architecture with abundant interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The structure of the hierarchical CoFe@NiFe-200/NF core-shell architecture was further confirmed by the TEM analysis (Fig. 2e). Compared with the smooth surface of CoFe-LDH nanosheet (Figure S3), many tiny nanosheets with thickness of around 6 nm were decorated on the surface to form hierarchical core-shell architectures with abundant interfaces (Fig. 2f).

nodes.characterization_summary: CoFe@NiFe-200/NF shows lattice fringes of 0.25 nm and 0.263 nm corresponding to (012) planes of CoFe-LDH and NiFe-LDH respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringes of 0.25 nm and 0.263 nm in Fig. 2g correspond to the (012) plane of CoFe-LDH and (012) plane of NiFe-LDH, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoFe@NiFe-200/NF shows Ni, Fe, Co, and O elements uniformly distributed throughout the structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images (Fig. 2h) demonstrate that the nickel, iron, cobalt and oxygen elements are uniformly distributed throughout the whole CoFe@NiFe-200/NF

The XRD patterns of as-preapred CoFe@NiFe core-shell architectures, bare CoFe-LDH/NF, and NiFe-LDH/NF are shown in Fig. 3a ... In the CoFe@NiFe-200/NF sample, all the diffraction peaks can be assigned either to the CoFe-LDH or to the NiFe-LDH, and no other impurity phase can be found

nodes.characterization_summary: CoFe-LDH: Co 2p3/2 780.8 eV, Co 2p1/2 796.7 eV (Co²⁺); Fe 2p3/2 710.5 eV, Fe 2p1/2 724.3 eV (Fe³⁺). CoFe@NiFe-200/NF shows negative shifts in Co (0.07-0.13 eV) and Fe (0.3-1.1 eV) peaks indicating strong interfacial electron interactions. NiFe-LDH: Ni 2p3/2 856.2 eV, Ni 2p1/2 873.8 eV (Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺); CoFe@NiFe-200/NF shows Ni peak shifts confirming electronic interactions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 3b, the high resolution spectra of Co 2p for CoFe-LDH shows the binding energies of Co 2p3/2 and Co 2p1/2 at 780.8 eV and 796.7 eV ... Comparably, the peaks of Co 2p3/2 and Co 2p1/2 of CoFe@NiFe-200/NF have a slightly negative shift by 0.07 and 0.13 eV ... the binding energies of Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 of the CoFe@NiFe-200/NF sample show a negative shift of 1.1 and 0.3 eV ... the two major peaks of NiFe-LDH located at binding energies of 856.2 and 873.8 eV
